classification.difficultyReason: Derive the dimensions of an inscribed square pyramid from a cone, then calculate its total surface area.

content.prompt: A woodworker uses a rotating lathe to produce a cone with radius $4\text{ cm}$ and height $20\text{ cm}$. From that cone the woodworker then cut slices off the sides of the cone to produce a square pyramid of the same height.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, shared figure beside parts a–b
spec.description: Unshaded cone enclosing a square pyramid with a common apex and base plane. The square is inscribed in the circular base. All four square sides have matching double ticks. External dimensions retain the 8 cm diameter and 20 cm perpendicular height. Ordinary source blue outlines become black; red dashed lines retain the distinction of the inscribed construction. This overlapping composite uses explicit pyramid faces and an analytic cone silhouette.
spec.mathematics: Cone radius 4 cm and perpendicular height 20 cm. Square vertices lie on the base circle at angles −60°, 30°, 120° and 210°. The square diagonal is the circle diameter, 8 cm. Projection uses right=(0.25,0,0), up=(0,0.075,0.125).
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, equality marks and construction geometry are visible; no derived lengths or answers are printed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the exact slant height of the cone.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the exact side length of the base of the square pyramid.

answer.worked:
The square's diagonal is the circle's diameter, $8\text{ cm}$. Let its side length be $s$.
$$\begin{align*}s^2+s^2&=8^2\\2s^2&=64\\s^2&=32\\s&=4\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the slant height of the pyramid, correct to 3 decimal places.

answer.worked:
The distance from the base centre to the midpoint of a side is $2\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$. Using Pythagoras' theorem for the face slant height $L$:
$$\begin{align*}L^2&=20^2+(2\sqrt{2})^2\\L^2&=408\\L&=\sqrt{408}\\L&\approx20.199\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the surface area of the pyramid, correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Add the square base and four triangular faces, using the unrounded slant height.
$$\begin{align*}A&=s^2+4\left(\frac12sL\right)\\A&=(4\sqrt{2})^2+4\left(\frac12(4\sqrt{2})\sqrt{408}\right)\\A&=32+32\sqrt{51}\\A&\approx260.53\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
